lines.japanese: 「ありがとうございました！　またのご来店をお待ちしております！」
lines.english: “Thank you very much! We hope to see you again!”

lines.japanese: 最後のお客さんが出ていかれ、店先の照明も落とすと、先んじて進めていた閉店準備にいよいよ拍車がかかります。
lines.english: Once the final customer had left and the lights outside were extinguished, the closing work we had begun earlier shifted into high gear.

lines.japanese: 先輩アルバイトの工藤さんは、埃を巻きあげる勢いでフロアに水モップをかけてまわっておりました。
lines.english: Kudo, one of the veteran part-timers, drove a wet mop across the floor fast enough to raise dust.

lines.japanese: と思ったら、ふと彼は舌打ちして足を止め、その場で執拗にモップを擦りはじめました。
lines.english: Then he clicked his tongue, stopped short, and began attacking one spot with dogged persistence.

lines.japanese: 「あー鷲介さー、悪い、なんてったっけアレ、ほらアレ──」
lines.english: “Hey, Shusuke. Sorry—what was that stuff called? You know, the stuff—”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、アレすか」
lines.english: “Oh, that?”

lines.japanese: 彼が空いてる方の手で示した、こぶしを上下に振るようなジェスチャーに気付いて、俺はすかさず所定の位置へ走りまた戻ってきました。
lines.english: He pumped his free fist up and down in demonstration. I caught his meaning, raced to the supply station, and came straight back.

lines.japanese: 「コレっすか？」
lines.english: “This?”

lines.japanese: こびりついたしつこい汚れに、クリームクレンザーとスチールウール。
lines.english: Cream cleanser and steel wool: the answer to stubborn, caked-on grime.

lines.japanese: 「そーそー、それそれ。ん～？　分かってきたじゃん」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah, that’s it. Hmm? You’re catching on.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、ここ俺やっときますんで」
lines.english: “I’ll take care of this spot.”

lines.japanese: 言いおわらないうちにさっさと屈んで、汚れの上にクレンザーをたら～り＆タワシでごしごしごしっ。
lines.english: Before the words were out, I was already crouching down: cleanser drizzled onto the stain, then scrub-scrub-scrub with the pad.

lines.japanese: 「お、ありがと。濯ぎはやっとくから」
lines.english: “Oh, thanks. I’ll rinse it afterward.”

lines.japanese: 「おいっす」
lines.english: “You got it.”

lines.japanese: こうして連携の取れたチームワークで、今日もクローズ作業は順調に進むのでした。
lines.english: And so, through seamless teamwork, the closing work proceeded smoothly once again.

lines.japanese: 心なしか工藤さんとも若干打ちとけてきた気がします。
lines.english: I felt as though Kudo and I had begun to warm to each other, if only a little.

lines.japanese: 「そういや鷲介、今日からフロア入ってたでしょ」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, Shusuke, you started on the floor today, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ああはい、そうなんすよ」
lines.english: “Oh, yes. That's right.”

lines.japanese: だから、ふたり近い距離で作業しているときには他愛もない会話が交わされたりします。
lines.english: So whenever our work brought us close together, we would trade a little idle chatter.

lines.japanese: 「いきなり土曜じゃ、客多くて大変だったんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Starting on a Saturday must’ve been rough. Lots of customers.”

lines.japanese: 「や、俺が入ったの、ランチタイム過ぎてからだったんすよ。夜に向けて少しずつ忙しくなってく感じで、わりとっつうか、ちょうどイイカンジでしたね」
lines.english: “I didn’t start until after lunch. Things just got steadily busier as dinner approached, so it was pretty—actually, it was just about perfect.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうなんだ」
lines.english: “Oh. I see.”

lines.japanese: 「むしろ、空いてる時間マスターの暇つぶしに付きあわされてる方のが大変だったり」
lines.english: “Honestly, being forced to entertain the boss whenever things were quiet might’ve been harder.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、そっか。そういや俺も入りたてのころは、よくあのおっさんにおちょくられてウザかったよ」
lines.english: “Haha. Yeah. When I first started, that old man used to mess with me all the time too. Drove me crazy.”

lines.japanese: 「あー……はー、そうなんすか……」
lines.english: “Oh... huh. Is that right...?”

lines.japanese: 「おっさん相変わらずだなあ。アレだろ、寒い下ネタ連発すんだろ？　アレさー、職場の雰囲気あっためようとして頑張ってんのは分かんだけど、逆に反応困んだよねー。なあー？」
lines.english: “He never changes. You know how he fires off one lame dirty joke after another? I can tell he’s trying to warm up the workplace, but it only makes it harder to know how to react. Right?”

lines.japanese: 「ねー、そっすよねえ。相手いちお店長っすもんねえ。露骨につまんない顔とか出来ないっすもんねえ」
lines.english: “Yeah. Exactly. He is the Manager, after all. You can’t exactly let your face say how unfunny he is.”

lines.japanese: 「だよなー」
lines.english: “Right?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもね？　なんか適当に相槌打ちながら聞いてたら、そのうちだんだん面白くなってきましたよ」
lines.english: “But you know, if you listen and make encouraging noises in the right places, eventually he actually starts getting funny.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　マジで？」
lines.english: “What? Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「あの、ほら、芸人でいるじゃないすか。初め全然なんだけど、ある日こっちのスイッチ入ったら急に笑けてくる系の。あんな感じ」
lines.english: “You know those comedians who do absolutely nothing for you at first, then one day a switch flips in your head and suddenly everything they say makes you laugh? Like that.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そーなん？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「マジす、マジす。基本、パワーでゴリゴリなんすけどね、たまに上手いこと言ったりしてんすよあのおっさん。試しにちょっと聞いといた方がいっすよ。何気にコンパとかで使えるネタ拾えますよ」
lines.english: “Seriously, seriously. Most of the time he just steamrolls through on raw power, but now and then the old man says something genuinely clever. You should give him a proper listen sometime. You can pick up material for mixers without even trying.”

lines.japanese: 「へえー、ほんとかねえ」
lines.english: “Huh. You really think so?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、ええ、わりかしマジで」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah. I’m actually pretty serious.”

lines.japanese: そして閉店作業を終えた俺は、工藤さんと別れて二階へ上がりました。
lines.english: Once the closing work was done, I parted from Kudo and went upstairs.

lines.japanese: 首をほぐし、襟元を緩めながら控え室の扉を開けると、合皮張りのソファーに若い娘さんが俯き加減で座っておいででした。
lines.english: Working the stiffness out of my neck and loosening my collar, I opened the staff-room door to find a young woman sitting on the imitation-leather sofa, her head bowed.

lines.japanese: 彼女は食後の大型獣みたいにのっそり頭をもたげると、ドアを背に立ちすくんでいた俺の姿を、あの温かくも冷たくもない目でじっと見上げました。
lines.english: She raised her head with the ponderous motion of a great beast after a meal, then fixed those eyes of hers—neither warm nor cold—on me as I stood frozen against the door.

lines.japanese: 「ひ、日和子さんお疲れさまです！」
lines.english: “H-Hiyoko! Good work today!”

lines.japanese: 一瞬および腰になりながらも、すぐに背を反らし顎まで反らせ、天井へ放つように声を張りあげる俺。
lines.english: I shrank back for a split second, then arched my spine, lifted my chin, and called out at the ceiling.

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは上唇と下唇を離してから数瞬の間を置き、やがて小さく息を吸いこんでから──わずかに頭を下げました。
lines.english: Hiyoko parted her lips. Several moments passed. At last she drew a small breath—then dipped her head by the slightest degree.

lines.japanese: 「お疲れさまです」
lines.english: “Good work today.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……い、いえ、とんでもございません」
lines.english: “Ah... n-no, it was nothing.”

lines.japanese: まさにとんでもないことをされた気分になって、俺も慌てて腰を折りまげました。
lines.english: It felt like anything but nothing. Flustered, I bent deeply at the waist myself.

lines.japanese: それからゆっくりと日和子さんはソファーから腰を上げ、俺もまた垂れていた頭を持ちあげました。
lines.english: Then Hiyoko slowly rose from the sofa, and I straightened up as well.

lines.japanese: 「それでは、お先に失礼します」
lines.english: “Good night. I’m heading out.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……はい」
lines.english: “Ah... yes.”
